verdict:
The licence core of the recommendation holds up. Owner-captured photos processed with MIT/Apache/GPL tools, CC0 inputs (iNaturalist, Poly Haven, ffishAsia), RealityScan under US$1M group revenue (EULA s.2(b)(i), s.6), private evaluation of paid assets (Maxtree EULA 2.1(1); Fab EULA 3(a), whose free Bigleaf Hydrangea is Standard License with fbx/gltf), and the PlantCatalog spruce as CC BY 4.0 from the official account all check out.

Several claims fail once the actual texts are read:
- Server-side Cycles is not a licence escape for paid assets. Maxtree and Fab both count online functionality as distribution and bar third parties using content inside tools that export works.
- Maxtree is "not allowed by default", not "unclear". Its 3.2 example names "other tools that allow exporting works", and 2.2(3) requires object/target code.
- The V3 Maxtree rebuild cannot be done by an external artist at Indie/Pro (2.3, 3.2), or by cloud AI agents (3.2 "prompt input" clause).
- A hired PlantFactory artist breaches e-on EULA s.5 ("may also not use the Software to provide fee or transaction-based services").
- The CC BY spruce would conflict with the site's existing Terms (src/pages/Terms.tsx:39) and with the planned anti-extraction ToU and encryption (CC BY 4.0 s.2(a)(5)(B)).
- The maksm Spiraea fallback is labelled "For educational purposes only", which PLAN.md had already blocked.

Minor gaps:
- The free Megascans Norway Maple is Unreal-format only, so it needs a UE EULA.
- Maxtree's Superhive editions fall under Superhive's Royalty Free licence.
- The copyleft clauses name GPL, and Blender is GPL.
- An AI-texture label kept only in a manifest does not reach homeowners.
- Marigold weights are OpenRAIL++-M.
- The licensee entity has to match whoever operates DeckCraft.

Not verified, because the web-search budget ran out mid-task (every finding below rests on pages fetched directly): SpeedTree/Unity terms, Xfrog, Evermotion and the Unreal Engine EULA. None of these is a recommended or bake-off route.

problems.claim: Route 7 / rendering_upgrades: server-side Cycles stills are 'the cleanest way to get paid photoreal assets into homeowner-facing images without licence or extraction risk'; 'Pixels-only delivery removes the extraction problem. Each asset licence must still allow commercial rendering.'
problems.problem: Delivering only pixels does not escape the two paid licences the synthesis relies on. Both define distribution to include making a Project's functionality available online. Both separately forbid letting third parties (homeowners) incorporate the content into their own projects through a tool that exports works. A homeowner composing a yard and receiving a rendered still or PDF is exactly that. The 'linear media' freedom covers renders the licensee makes and distributes, not a rendering service for third parties' own designs.
problems.evidence:
Maxtree EULA (https://maxtree.org/eula/, updated 5 Mar 2026):
- 2.2(1): "'Distribute' means providing copies of a Project to the public/other individuals/entities, or making Project functionality available online."
- 3.2: you must not "Allow any third party to incorporate the content into its own products/services/projects (e.g., providing content in level editors, templates, modeling tools, or other tools that allow exporting works)."

Fab EULA (https://www.fab.com/eula):
- 4(a): "'Distribute' means ... make the Project's functionality available on a network."
- 6(b)(iii): you may not "allow any third party to incorporate Content into their own products, services, or other projects (this means, for example, that you may not make Content available in world- or level-editing tools or templates or other modeling tools that allow works to be exported)."
problems.fix: Rewrite route 7: server-side rendering removes the EXTRACTION risk only. It does not license homeowner-driven rendering of Maxtree or Fab content; that needs the vendor's written exception. Restrict route 7 to owner-captured, commissioned (with assignment), CC0 or CC BY assets, or to marketplace terms that expressly allow platform users to create content. For example, CGTrader Royalty Free s.21A.2 lists 'creators of ... applications or platforms if Product is provided to users ... to create embedded content' (https://www.cgtrader.com/pages/terms-and-conditions), subject to the s.21A.3 protection measures.

problems.claim: Route 5 (Maxtree): licence status 'Unclear for DeckCraft' ... 'DeckCraft is a design tool, though it exports only stills, video and PDF'. Shipping is possible from a non-public origin in an encrypted container, plus 2-4 dev-days for the container and loader.
problems.problem: Under the default-to-not-allowed rule this is not unclear; it is prohibited. Maxtree's own example list ends with 'other tools that allow exporting works', and DeckCraft exports works (stills, video, PDF). Separately, 2.2(3) allows end users the content only 'in object/target code form' with no source files. A GLB/glTF decoded in the browser (even with meshopt/KTX2, and after any JS decryption) is an open interchange format that the client must decode into usable vertex and texture data. Fab 4(c) has the same object-code wording. Spending on purchases or the container before a written exception arrives is wasted.
problems.evidence:
Maxtree EULA (https://maxtree.org/eula/):
- 3.2: "Allow any third party to incorporate the content into its own products/services/projects (e.g., providing content in level editors, templates, modeling tools, or other tools that allow exporting works)."
- 2.2(3): "End users may only use the content in the Project in object/target code form; you must not provide source files to end users."

Fab EULA 4(c): "only authorize end users to make use of Content solely as incorporated in the Project in object code" (https://www.fab.com/eula).

Note: the 3.2 bullets are unnumbered on the page, so the synthesis's 's.3.2(3)/(4)' numbering is inferred.
problems.fix: Change route 5's licence_status to 'NOT allowed for live runtime without Maxtree's written exception'. Quote the 3.2 'tools that allow exporting works' example and 2.2(3) 'object/target code' in the outreach. Do not budget the 2-4 dev-day encrypted container, or any Maxtree purchase for shipping, until the written exception exists. Private bake-off use under 2.1(1) stays OK.

problems.claim: Bake-off V3 and route 5: Maxtree packs are rebuilt in Blender in 'About 2 agent- or artist-days' (route 5: 'about 0.5-1 artist-day per species', 'Rebuild about 12-25 artist-days'), priced at Indie/Pro/Enterprise.
problems.problem:
Two clauses restrict who may do the rebuild.
(a) At Indie or Pro, licensed content cannot go to an external artist or contractor. Only Enterprise allows collaborators, and only under a written agreement, and derivative content must stay within the licensee's internal team.
(b) Maxtree forbids using its content as prompt input to any generative AI program, and uploading it to a third-party cloud AI service. A Claude agent reading Maxtree textures, meshes or files, or plausibly screenshots of them, is cloud generative-AI prompt input.
So neither an external freelancer (below Enterprise) nor the AI agents may do the V3 rebuild. Fab's NoAI clause covers datasets, development and training only, so it does not create the same bar for V4.
problems.evidence:
Maxtree EULA (https://maxtree.org/eula/):
- 2.3: "Under the Standard License, you may not distribute content to third parties on a standalone basis. However, the Enterprise license allows you to distribute licensed content to collaborators provided that ... You must sign a written agreement with collaborators".
- 3.2: "Allow derivative content to be used outside the purchasing licensee and its internal team directly serving it".
- 3.2: "Use code/content extracted from licensed products as training input or prompt input for any generative AI program ... it is strictly prohibited to upload such categorized datasets to any third-party cloud or AI service platform."

Fab EULA 16(l)(i) limits NoAI to "(a) in datasets utilized by Generative AI Programs, (b) in the development of Generative AI Programs, or (c) as training inputs".
problems.fix: V3 must be rebuilt by a human on the licensee's own staff (or by an external artist only under Enterprise with a written collaborator agreement), using local scripts that never pass Maxtree files or renders into an AI agent's context. Agents may only consume locally computed metrics. Alternatively, get Maxtree's written OK for agent-assisted processing. Re-cost V3 and route 5 labour on that basis.

problems.claim: Route 3 (PlantFactory): 'Approve an artist (in-house or hired)' / 'Hiring a PlantFactory artist is a spend'. Route 4: commission 'a freelancer working in PlantFactory'. e-on EULA s.2.2 makes scratch-built models public-repo and web OK; just 'Keep PlantCatalog metanodes and textures out.'
problems.problem: The free e-on EULA forbids using the software to provide fee-based services, so a hired or freelance artist billing Golden Maple for PlantFactory work breaches s.5. The EULA is also the entire agreement (s.14). 'Software' includes PlantFactory itself (s.1.5), and s.6 bars distributing the Software 'in part'. Bentley's permissive FAQ ('You may retexture, remodel and resell any of the stock content which ships with VUE and PlantFactory') is therefore not binding. Under default-not-allowed, PlantFactory's bundled stock leaf, bark and preset content is as risky as PlantCatalog.
problems.evidence:
e-on EULA (https://www.bentley.com/globalassets/content/eula-for-e-on-products.pdf):
- s.5: "User may not rent, lease, lend, or provide commercial hosting services with the Software. User may also not use the Software to provide fee or transaction-based services."
- s.1.5: "'Software' means VUE, PlantFactory, and PlantCatalog provided for free download."
- s.6: "Any reproduction ... or distribution by any means whatsoever of the Software, in part or in full, without the prior written permission from Bentley is strictly forbidden."
- s.14: "This EULA incorporates the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes and merges all prior oral and written agreements, discussions, and understandings".

FAQ wording from https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/.
problems.fix: Limit route 3 to Golden Maple's own staff running PlantFactory, or get Bentley's written permission (Eon-Questions@Bentley.com) for a paid contractor. Remove 'freelancer working in PlantFactory' from route 4; freelancers should use Blender or other tools whose terms permit fee-based work. Require scratch builds with owner-captured textures only, with no PlantFactory stock leaf, bark or preset content, unless Bentley confirms the FAQ in writing.

problems.claim: Route 6 / blue spruce: PlantCatalog 'Koster' CC BY 4.0 — 'public repo and web OK with attribution and an indication of changes'; owner action 'Add ATTRIBUTION.md entries'. Elsewhere, paid assets need 'site Terms of Use forbidding extraction' and an 'obfuscated or encrypted container'.
problems.problem: CC BY 4.0 forbids imposing extra terms on, or applying technological measures to, the licensed material. The site's live Terms already claim all site content and forbid copying or commercial use without written permission, so serving the CC BY spruce on the site imposes additional terms on it. The planned anti-extraction ToU and encrypted containers would add to the conflict if they cover the spruce. Attribution only in a repo ATTRIBUTION.md also does not reach visitors who receive the GLB from the website.
problems.evidence:
- CC BY 4.0 s.2(a)(5)(B) (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.en): "You may not offer or impose any additional or different terms or conditions on, or apply any Effective Technological Measures to, the Licensed Material if doing so restricts exercise of the Licensed Rights by any recipient of the Licensed Material." s.3(a)(1) requires the creator credit, licence notice/URI and an indication of modifications whenever the material is shared.
- src/pages/Terms.tsx:39: "All content on the Site ... is owned by Golden Maple Landscaping or used under license. ... you may not copy, republish, or use our content commercially without written permission."
- The Sketchfab page (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0) shows "License: CC Attribution".
problems.fix:
Before shipping any CC BY asset:
- Add a carve-out to Terms.tsx: third-party assets under open licences are governed by those licences and are not covered by this section.
- Keep CC BY files out of any encrypted container and out of any anti-extraction clause.
- Publish a site-visible credits/attributions page (title, author, source URL, licence URL, changes made) linked from DeckCraft, in addition to ATTRIBUTION.md.

problems.claim: Route 6 lists 'Spiraea japonica (maksm, 291k)' as merely provenance-unverified CC BY, and the per_species spirea fallback says 'maksm CC BY Spiraea japonica (291k faces) as a bake source'.
problems.problem: The model page carries a use restriction that contradicts its CC BY label. Under the default-to-not-allowed rule it is not licence-clean, even as a bake source for shipped textures or geometry. PLAN.md had already blocked it, so the synthesis regresses that decision. A second listed CC BY fallback, Gerhald's Thuja, also shows an aggregator red flag: its description advertises a third-party store and a model aggregator, which casts doubt on whether the uploader owns the copyright.
problems.evidence:
- Sketchfab page (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/9e1cf9580df9448bb576150022b716b0, checked 2026-10-17): "This wood model was created in the frame of the project APPLAUSE ... For educational purposes only. Additional info contact: maks.merela@bf.uni-lj.si." alongside "License: CC Attribution".
- PLAN.md:472: "Blocked, not offered: maksm 'Spiraea japonica' ... It stays blocked unless the owner obtains written commercial-use clearance from the author".
- Gerhald Thuja (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/33bf4b5dec10498faa13fcdc9ead6d4d), description: "Explore the Evolve Studio 3D Models Store ... visit CGHUB.one - world`s first 3d-model aggregator platform."
problems.fix: Remove the maksm Spiraea from route 6 and from the spirea fallback unless the author gives written commercial-use clearance (owner outreach). Use the ffishAsia CC0 Spiraea scans or owner capture instead. Treat the Gerhald Thuja as blocked, not just 'provenance unverified', until the uploader proves authorship.

problems.claim: Bake-off V4: 'Free Bigleaf Hydrangea ..., free Norway Maple ... Owner approval of an Epic account and the Fab EULA'.
problems.problem: The free Megascans Norway Maple is offered only in Unreal Engine format. Getting it into the Blender/three.js pipeline requires installing Unreal Engine and accepting the Unreal Engine EULA. The synthesis says that EULA was not reviewed, and it is missing from the V4 approval list. Only the Bigleaf Hydrangea ships as fbx/gltf.
problems.evidence:
- Norway Maple listing (https://www.fab.com/listings/1f65d477-f44e-4ccb-95c1-788c99e33b56): "Included formats: Unreal Engine", "Unreal Engine versions 5.1 – 5.6", "Distribution method: Asset package", "License terms: Standard License", "Free".
- Bigleaf Hydrangea listing (https://www.fab.com/listings/b8220edc-bf7f-4ab4-8618-3ae8209ac433): "Included formats fbx gltf", Standard License, Free.
- Synthesis cloud-streaming route: "Unreal EULA not reviewed."
problems.fix: Either drop the Norway Maple from V4 (use an fbx/gltf Megascans tree reference instead), or add an explicit approval: 'install Unreal Engine 5.x and accept the Unreal Engine EULA (to be reviewed first)'. List the download size, per the download rule.

problems.claim: Route 5 cost line: 'Superhive Blender editions US$175 per volume' (presented under the Maxtree EULA analysis).
problems.problem: Products bought on Superhive are licensed under Superhive's licence types, not the Maxtree EULA. Superhive's Royalty Free licence has no app/runtime distribution allowance and bars redistribution without the creator's permission. Buying the Superhive edition therefore changes the governing licence, and the Maxtree 2.2(3) object-code route analysis does not apply.
problems.evidence:
- Superhive help (https://support.superhivemarket.com/article/226-understanding-product-license-types): "All asset-based products are licensed under either Standard Royalty Free" or CC-BY 4.0.
- Superhive Royalty Free licence (https://superhivemarket.com/page/royalty-free-license): "You may not resell, redistribute, or repackage the purchased product without explicit permission from the original creator".
problems.fix: Mark the Superhive editions as 'Superhive Royalty Free: private use only; runtime/web use needs the creator's written permission'. For any shipping scenario, buy from maxtree.org under the Maxtree EULA (after the written exception).

problems.claim: V3/V4 rebuilds 'In Blender 5.2', and route 7 headless Blender Cycles with paid assets, are treated as licence-neutral.
problems.problem: Both paid EULAs bar combining or using Standard-License content with copyleft-licensed code and name GPL as the typical example. Blender, and bpy scripts run inside it, are GPL. The qualifier ('licenses that ... require the content to be subject to terms outside this Agreement') probably exempts Blender, whose GPL does not reach asset data. Maxtree, however, tells licensees to ask first when unsure, so under the default-to-not-allowed rule this needs confirmation.
problems.evidence:
- Maxtree EULA 3.1 (https://maxtree.org/eula/): "You must not (and must not allow others to) combine, distribute, or use content licensed under the Standard License with code/content governed by other licenses that directly or indirectly require the content to be subject to terms outside this Agreement ... Typical prohibited licenses include: GNU General Public License (GPL) ... If you are unsure whether a license is compatible, contact MAXTREE in advance."
- Fab EULA 6(a) (https://www.fab.com/eula) has equivalent wording naming GPL, LGPL and CC BY-SA.
problems.fix: Add 'processing in Blender (GPL) and headless Blender rendering' to the written questions for Maxtree. Keep DeckCraft's runtime free of GPL, LGPL and CC BY-SA code or assets; the current runtime dependencies checked are MIT/Apache/ISC/Unlicense plus clipper-lib, which declares 'BSL' and should be confirmed as Boost, not BUSL.

problems.claim: Route 11 (AI atlas sheets): 'Google bars presenting AI content as human-made to deceive; label it in the manifest.'
problems.problem: The audience who could be misled is the homeowner, not someone reading the repo. DeckCraft's stated goal is that homeowners cannot tell the plants from photos. The route-2 pitch is 'what you see is what we plant' with photographic texels of the exact cultivar. A label that exists only in species-manifest.json does not reach the people the Google and OpenAI clauses protect.
problems.evidence:
- Google Terms of Service, effective July 30, 2026 (https://policies.google.com/terms), prohibit "misleading others into thinking that generative AI content was created by a human".
- OpenAI Terms of Use, effective 1 Jan 2026 (https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/), prohibit representing "that Output was human-generated when it was not".
problems.fix: While any AI-derived sheet ships, add a user-visible note in DeckCraft's plant info and credits (e.g. 'some interim plant textures are AI-assisted and will be replaced with our own photos'). Keep 'what you see is what we plant' marketing off species that still use AI sheets.

problems.claim: Route 2: 'AI is used only as processing tools: BiRefNet MIT matting, Meshroom photometric-stereo normals, Marigold albedo', with a list of 'Licence-clean tools' that gives no licence for Marigold.
problems.problem: The Marigold model weights are not under the code repository's Apache-2.0 licence; they are under CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M. That licence allows commercial use but adds use-based restrictions and must be recorded correctly in the provenance chain. A planner copying 'Apache-2.0' from the GitHub repo would record the wrong licence.
problems.evidence:
- Hugging Face model metadata (https://huggingface.co/api/models/prs-eth/marigold-iid-appearance-v1-1 and .../marigold-iid-lighting-v1-1): license "openrail++".
- The GitHub repo prs-eth/Marigold declares Apache-2.0 for code only.
- BiRefNet weights (ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet, BiRefNet_HR-matting) are MIT, and Depth-Anything-V2-Small is apache-2.0; both confirmed.
problems.fix: Record Marigold IID weights as 'CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M (outputs usable commercially; use-based restrictions apply)' in the tool provenance list, and pin the exact checkpoint used.

problems.claim: Paid-route pricing and eligibility: owner 'Confirm the revenue tier'; Fab Personal 'measured on DIGITAL-CONTENT revenue only'.
problems.problem: The licence must be bought by the same legal entity that operates DeckCraft. Maxtree Indie/Pro grants do not extend to affiliates, and derivative content cannot be used by parent, sister or group companies. Fab's Personal-tier test aggregates every entity under common control. DeckCraft runs on goldenmaplelandscaping.ca, while the DeckCraft Pro sign-up lives at goldenmaplegroup.com/pro (Golden Maple Group). A licence bought by one Golden Maple entity may not cover use by the other.
problems.evidence:
- Maxtree EULA 1.2 (https://maxtree.org/eula/): Indie and Pro "grants rights to a single entity only and does not extend to affiliates, partners, subsidiaries, and/or entities with the same parent company name". 2.4: "Only the authorized licensee may use it; it does not include affiliates, parent companies, subsidiaries, branches, or group companies".
- Fab EULA 2(a) (https://www.fab.com/eula): Personal only if "you, together with any controlling entity and other entities under common control with you, have not generated more than $100,000 USD in gross revenue from your commercial activity in the digital content industry".
problems.fix: Add an open question: which legal entity operates DeckCraft, including Pro? Buy any evaluation or shipping licence in that entity's name. For Fab, count the whole group's digital revenue (SaaS lines included) when choosing Personal or Professional. For Maxtree, use the group's total revenue, which likely means Enterprise.
